title: Rules That Change the Rules: Everything Popular Is Wrong
coreMove: Treat popular rules as guesses; run small opposite tests where the crowd is unhappy, the downside is repairable, and results can be counted.

exampleSpecs.stakes: reach the buyer or keep polishing a blocked script
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the protagonist tests timing instead of competing inside the normal calling window

exampleSpecs.audience: students choosing between prestige and autonomy
exampleSpecs.stakes: accept a default career path or test whether it fits the life desired
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the protagonist treats prestige as a default path, not proof of fit

exampleSpecs.audience: teams assuming effort means more of the same hours
exampleSpecs.stakes: find donors directly or exhaust volunteers in blocked windows
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the protagonist changes timing to reach decision-makers

exampleSpecs.audience: employees waiting for approval on low-risk experiments
exampleSpecs.stakes: seek permission indefinitely or run a repairable test
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the protagonist distinguishes reversible action from reckless rule-breaking

exampleSpecs.audience: account teams mistaking busyness for better odds
exampleSpecs.stakes: measure an opposite schedule or keep rewarding visible effort
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the protagonist measures whether unusual timing beats the common schedule

exampleSpecs.audience: high achievers choosing only crowded moderate goals
exampleSpecs.stakes: pick a safe crowded target or test a stranger aim with fewer rivals
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the protagonist sees that unreasonable goals may have less competition
